## What's new in 0.1.1
This version adds two parts to the GUI's **Settings** > **System**: **Current configuration**, which shows what the console's **View Config** shows, and **Campground data**, which refreshes the campground list from the GUI and then restarts Campertron to use it. The GUI also says more clearly which searches run where: a search is now **Enabled (autoRun)** or **Not enabled**. The console works as before, except that a refresh of the campground list no longer waits forever for a download that has stopped. Your settings, search files, campground list, `Camp.History` and theme choice are kept and need no changes.

### See your current configuration in the GUI
- **Settings** > **System** > **Current configuration** shows the same eight values as the console's **View Config**: the version, the settings and cache folders, where results go, how many search files there are, when the campground list was last refreshed, and the operating system and .NET version.
- It only shows them: it never changes a file, and it never shows anything of `Email.yaml` or the contents of your search files.
- **Copy** puts the values on the clipboard as text, for example for a bug report, and **Open settings folder** shows the settings folder in your file manager.

### Refresh the campground list in the GUI
- **Settings** > **System** > **Campground data** shows when the campground list was last refreshed. **Refresh campground data…** downloads recreation.gov's latest list (about 570 MB) and builds a new campground list from it, as the console's **Refresh Ridb Data (slow)** does. It can take several minutes; your settings and search files stay as they are.
- Nothing starts until you confirm with **Start refresh**; **Back** changes nothing.
- While it runs, the card shows each step, the progress where its size is known and the elapsed time. **Cancel** stops it until the new data is being installed; from then on the refresh finishes safely, even if you close Campertron.
- A search in the **Results** tab and a refresh don't run at the same time: while one runs, the other is unavailable.

### Campertron restarts itself after a refresh
- After a successful refresh, Campertron restarts by itself to load the new campground list and opens again at **Settings** > **System**, in the same place and size on the screen (maximized if it was) when your system allows it. It keeps the window's place only for this one restart; later starts open as usual.
- If **Settings** or **Searches** have unsaved changes, Campertron doesn't restart, so nothing is lost: save or revert them, then restart Campertron yourself.
- If the restart fails, the new campground list stays installed; restart Campertron yourself to use it.

### Clearer words for which searches run
- In the GUI a search is now **Enabled (autoRun)** or **Not enabled**, instead of "Run this search (autoRun)", "Runs at startup", "Not run at startup", "Enabled" and "Disabled". The setting in your search files is still `autoRun`, and nothing in them changes.
- The console runs only enabled searches: its **Search** reads your search files each time you choose it, and email mode reads them once, when it starts, and then checks the enabled searches every minute, so restart email mode after you change a search.
- The **Results** tab selects the enabled searches that can be searched by default. A search that is not enabled is listed unselected and runs when you select it, without changing the file.
- Starting the GUI never runs a search. The GUI's messages no longer say that a search runs "at startup" or that the example search is created at Campertron's next start: while there is no search file, the console creates its example search the next time it searches (when you choose **Search** or start email mode).

### More reliable refreshes of the campground list
- A refresh, from the GUI, the console's menu or the automatic refresh at start (`autoRefresh: true`), now ends with an error when no data has arrived for 60 seconds, instead of waiting forever for a download that has stopped. The installed campground list is not changed.
- The download now goes into a folder of its own, `CampertronDownload-` followed by a random code, next to the `CampertronConfig` folder, and Campertron removes it afterwards, also after a failure or a cancel; the next refresh removes one that an interrupted refresh left behind. Before, it went straight to `RIDBFullExport_V1_JSON.zip` in that place, and a file of that name was deleted first.
- Otherwise the console's refresh shows the same lines as before; only its "Extracting" line names the new folder.

### Checks before publishing
- The GUI's built-in smoke test, which the release workflow runs on each platform it starts before publishing, now also checks the **Current configuration** and **Campground data** cards without pressing their buttons, so it never downloads the campground list, and that the GUI finds its own program for the automatic restart, without restarting.

## Upgrading from 0.1.0
- **Desktop:** extract the new archives and use them instead of your old Campertron folders. Your settings, searches, campground list, `Camp.History` and theme choice are kept and need no changes.
- **Docker:** change the image tag to `0.1.1`, or pull `0.1` or `latest` again, which now point to this version, and recreate the container with the same `/config` and `/cache` mounts. `0.1` and `latest` only ever move forward to a newer stable version, and `0.1.0` stays on 0.1.0.
- **Your search files:** nothing to change. **Enabled (autoRun)** and **Not enabled** are new names in the GUI for the same `autoRun` setting.
- **A file an older version may have left:** if a refresh of an earlier version was interrupted or failed, `RIDBFullExport_V1_JSON.zip` (about 570 MB) may still be next to your `CampertronConfig` folder. This version neither uses nor deletes it; you can delete it.
- To check your download, use the checksums and build attestations described under "Verify your download" below.

## Upgrading from an earlier version
Follow the steps above, and read "Upgrading from an earlier version" in the [0.1.0 notes](https://github.com/ShaunAnthonyHathaway/Campertron/releases/tag/v0.1.0): it lists what changed before 0.1.0 that can affect you, such as how filters with several values match.

## Known limitations
- **A refresh needs free disk space.** With recreation.gov's list of November 17, 2026, the folder that holds `CampertronConfig` needed up to about 1.15 GB more than the installed campground list while the refresh ran (measured on Linux), and the database engine also uses some space in your system's temporary folder. Campertron doesn't check the free space before it starts.
- **The refresh and the automatic restart on Windows and macOS.** Both were run in a real window only on Linux. On Windows and macOS the checks before publishing confirm that the GUI finds its own program to restart, but they don't refresh or restart it. Whether the window reopens in its old place and size depends on your system's window manager; this was checked with one, KWin on Linux.
- **The GUI on Windows and macOS.** Before publishing, the GUI is started on Windows and macOS and runs its built-in checks there, including its light and dark themes, a campground's filter values and the two new cards of **Settings** > **System**. Those checks don't cover how the tabs look, keyboard use or screen readers, or whether **System** follows the theme setting of Windows and macOS.
- **Console on Windows and macOS.** The console's layout, colors and menu had a manual visual check on Windows, not a complete test, and haven't been tried on macOS.
- **Checking hundreds of filter values before saving.** Each change re-checks every value you added since the last save, so after checking all 360 campsites of a large campground, each further change takes about a second until you save.
- **The Results tab can take a few minutes when recreation.gov doesn't answer.** A month is asked for up to three times, with a wait of 30 seconds after a failed request, before it is listed as "not checked". **Cancel** ends the wait at once.
- **Searching one campground for the first time in two Campertron programs at once** can make one of the searches stop with an error, because both prepare the campground's site details at the same moment. This has not been seen in testing; if it happens, run the search again.
- **Email mode keeps running without any search to run.** If none of your search files is enabled (`autoRun: true`), email mode warns once and then reports "0 searches" at every check.
- **Email clients not yet checked.** The results page was checked in Chrome and Firefox on Linux, but no test email was sent, so its appearance in Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail is unverified. Each email contains the page twice (as the body and as the attachment), so a search with thousands of results can make a large email that some providers may reject.
- **Your email password is stored as plain text** in `Email.yaml`, which gets your system's usual file permissions when Campertron's first start creates it, and the README's Docker steps make the settings folder writable for every user of the computer. This matters on a computer that other people can sign in to.
- **The included campground list is recreation.gov's data of November 10, 2026.** Campsites added since then are not reported until you refresh the list, with **Refresh campground data…** in the GUI or **Refresh Ridb Data (slow)** in the console (see "Keep the campground list up to date" in the README).
- Avalonia, the GUI's UI framework, lists 32-bit Windows (`win-x86`) as a commercially supported platform only and doesn't list 32-bit ARM Linux desktops (`linux-arm`). The 32-bit Windows downloads are started on 64-bit Windows before publishing, not on a 32-bit system, and the `linux-arm` downloads are built but not started.
